items.stem: Which protocol is commonly used for lightweight device messaging with AWS IoT Core?

options.rationale: Correct: MQTT is a lightweight pub/sub protocol used by IoT devices.
SMTP is for email, not device telemetry.
SNMP is network management, not the IoT Core device protocol.
FTP is file transfer, not IoT messaging.

items.explanation: Correct: MQTT is the lightweight IoT messaging protocol.

items.stem: Which TWO practices secure device connections at scale? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Issue a unique certificate per device
options.rationale: Correct: per-device certs limit blast radius if one is compromised.

options.text: Attach least-privilege IoT policies scoping allowed topics
options.rationale: Correct: scoped policies restrict what a device can do.

options.text: Reuse one certificate for all devices
options.rationale: A shared cert is a security risk.

options.text: Allow every device to publish to every topic
options.rationale: Over-broad topic access violates least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: per-device certs and scoped policies secure the fleet.

items.stem: What does a device shadow store?

options.text: The desired and reported state of a device, persisted in the cloud
options.rationale: Correct: shadows hold state so apps can read/set it even when the device is offline.
Shadows store state, not firmware images.
That is logging, not the shadow.
Shadows do not store billing information.

items.explanation: Correct: a shadow stores desired/reported device state.
